sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the commercial centre of Keyport, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. It runs from the Raritan Bay shore, which crosses the top of the sheet, south to West Cross and 3rd Street (Cross) East at the foot, and from Main Street at the left to Osborn Street at the right. Broad Street and Division Street run down the middle of the sheet and meet Front Street West and Front Street East, the principal business street, about two thirds of the way down. North of Front Street the blocks are crowded with brick and frame stores, the Raritan Hotel, the Raritan Inn, the Mansion House and the Monmouth Hotel, with the Jersey Central Traction office and a boarding house, a dancing pavilion and a bath house along the shore at the right, and a sewerage disposal works with a septic tank and gas engine pump near the bay at the left. Broad Street and 1st Street East run obliquely across this northern part, and the bay shore is a heavy line with blue water tint, with a compass rose in the open water. South of Front Street the blocks hold the Peoples National Bank, the post office, a telephone exchange, drug stores, a chemical company fire department, St. Mary's Episcopal Church with its Sunday school, the 1st Presbyterian Church, the Fire Department Raritan Hose Company, Schank's Garage with a capacity of 35 cars, the 1st Baptist Church and a number of private garages. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn along the streets with hydrants at the corners. Street widths are lettered: 30 feet on West Cross, 40 feet on 3rd Street East and Division, 50 feet on Main, Broad and Front. The top margin carries the numbers of sheets 12 and 3, the left margin sheet 6 and the foot sheet 4.
notes: Front Street West and Front Street East are today West Front Street and East Front Street; West Cross is today West 3rd Street, and 3rd Street (Cross) East is today 3rd Street.
Main, Broad, Division and Osborn are today Main Street, Broad Street, Division Street and Osborn Street.
The modern node at Division Street and East Front Street lies about 10 m west of the junction as drawn, so it was left out of the control.
West Front Street at Main Street is displaced from the drawn junction by about 11 m in the modern data and was left out.
Broad Street and 1st Street East north of Front Street run obliquely and no junction there was used as control.
50 ft, one part. Front St (W./E.), Main to Osborn, W. Cross/3rd (Cross) to the bay; Broad and 1st St E run obliquely north of Front. Adjoins sheet 12 part 2.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the east side of central Keyport, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. The Raritan Bay shore, a heavy line with blue water tint and a small creek mouth at the right, crosses the top of the sheet. 1st Street East runs obliquely across the upper part, lined on its bay side with frame dwellings, a few stores and a boarding house; below it Front East crosses the sheet from the left margin to Church Street, with the Armory Hall, the Town Hall with the Fire Department Hook and Ladder Company, and a row of brick stores at its western end. Osborn Street, Church Street and Atlantic Street run down the sheet, Osborn and Church bending slightly as they go, and John Street and 2nd Street cross them at an angle. The Keyport Shirt Factory with a lodge hall above, the West Furniture Company warehouse and the Conover Lumber Company yard and storage buildings are the principal industrial and commercial premises, and Calvary M. E. Church with its Sunday school and tower stands near the foot. The blocks south of Front East are otherwise small frame dwellings with outbuildings on narrow lots, and the part of the sheet right of Atlantic Street is blank, belonging to sheet 10. The foot of the sheet is 3rd Street (Cross) East with a scale bar below it. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn along the streets. Street widths of 30, 40 and 50 feet are lettered. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 2, 12, 13, 11 and 10, and a compass rose stands at the upper right.
notes: Front East is today East Front Street, and 3rd Street (Cross) East is today 3rd Street.
Osborn, Church and Atlantic are today Osborn Street, Church Street and Atlantic Street.
John Street is not in the modern street data and was not used as control.
The modern 2nd Street / Atlantic Street junction is about 1.5 m from a fit to the other points and sits roughly 15 ft north of the drawn 2nd Street pipe.
50 ft, one part. East Front St, Osborn, Church, Atlantic, John, 1st/2nd/3rd St E; bay at top.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers six blocks in the centre of Keyport, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. It runs from West Cross and 3rd Street (Cross) at the top to Maple Place (West Mott) at the bottom, and from Main Street on the left to Osborn Street on the right, with Broad Street and Division Street running through the middle and West and East Warren and West and East Elizabeth crossing them. The blocks are almost entirely residential: frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys on deep lots, with rows of small auto garages and sheds along the rear lot lines and a few brick-veneered or tile houses shown in pink. The institutional buildings are a public library at the corner of Broad Street and 3rd Street, the Reformed Church with a separate social hall on the block between Division and Osborn north of East Elizabeth Street, and the large brick public school, with steam heat and gas and electric lights, that fills most of the block between Broad and Division south of East Elizabeth. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are drawn along every street with hydrants at the corners. House numbers are given in both the current and the older series (older numbers in brackets). Street widths are lettered: 30 feet on West Cross, 40 feet on Warren and Division, 50 feet on Main, Broad and Elizabeth. The margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets: 2 above, 6 to the left, 10 to the right and 9 below. The lower part of the sheet shows open rear yards with no buildings over much of the block south of East Elizabeth.
notes: West Cross is today West 3rd Street; 3rd Street (Cross) east of Broad is 3rd Street.
Maple Place carries the older name West Mott in brackets.
Main, Broad, Division and Osborn are today Main Street, Broad Street, Division Street and Osborn Street; Warren and Elizabeth are Warren Street and Elizabeth Street.
Stout Street is lettered in the left margin as a pointer to sheet 6.
50 ft. Pilot. Main to Osborn, W. Cross/3rd St (Cross) to Maple Pl (W. Mott); one part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the west side of Keyport, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. A broad bundle of streets runs obliquely from the top right of the sheet to the lower left: Theress, Washington, Broadway, Chingarora Avenue and Luppatatong Avenue, crossed by Front Street West, West 2nd Street, 1st Street, 3rd Street, 4th Street, Provost, Chandler, Hobart and, at the foot, Maple Place and a second Washington Street with the lettered notes Not Opened and Not Named on streets laid out but not yet built. The district is a recently platted suburb: long, narrow numbered lots (blocks numbered 35, 36, 139 to 158, 205, 206, 214, 215, 219 and 225) with scattered frame dwellings and only a few pink brick buildings, among them a public school, No. 3, on Broadway near West 2nd Street and a fire hose house near 1st Street at the upper right. A garage and an oyster house stand beside Front Street West at the top. A bottling plant stands on Broadway near Chingarora Avenue, a service station sits at the foot of the sheet on Washington Street, and a bridge is lettered where a road crosses Luppatatong Creek at the lower right. Matawan Creek crosses the upper left corner, and the rest of the upper left is blank, with a compass rose. Street widths of 40, 50, 60 and 75 feet are lettered. Dashed lines show the drawn lot lines and 4 and 6 inch water pipes run along the principal streets. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 6 to the upper right and 7 below, and the printed scale bar stands at the foot.
notes: Theress is today Therese Avenue.
West 2nd Street, 1st Street (west of Broadway) are today West 2nd Street and West 1st Street; 1st Street between Chingarora and Luppatatong Avenues is Northwest 1st Street.
Washington, Broadway, Chandler, Provost and Hobart are today Washington Street, Broadway, Chandler Avenue, Provost Avenue and Hobart Street.
Chandler Avenue does not cross Broadway on the sheet although the modern data has a junction there; it was left out of the control.
The streets lettered Not Opened and Not Named at the foot of the sheet are not in the modern data.
The fit puts px_per_ft at about 3.99 against the expected 4.0 for a 100 ft sheet.
100 ft, one part. Theress (Therese Av), Washington, Broadway, Chandler, Provost, Hobart, Chingarora and Luppatatong Avs, Front St W, 1st-5th Sts; Chandler does not cross Broadway.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 covers the west end of Keyport's business district and the blocks south of it between Luppatatong Creek and Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. Front Street West runs across the top beside Raritan Bay and crosses Luppatatong Creek on a bridge at the left. Its bay side carries the waterfront businesses: the coal sheds and oyster house of the J. and J. W. Elsworth Company, C. C. Galbraith and Son marine supplies, the boat shops of New Jersey Motors Inc., the Keyport Boat Works at the bridge and a row of oyster houses on the creek. On the inland side of Front Street are stores, an auto repair and service garage, the Surf Theatre, the Keyport Weekly printing office, the Dawson House and the E. E. Cline marble and granite works. South of Front Street Beers and Kearney run down to Maple Place (West Mott), crossed by Barnes, Stout, Short and West Elizabeth, with Main Street along the right edge; these blocks are filled with frame dwellings and small garages. The left half of the sheet below Front Street is the wide loop of Luppatatong Creek and the open block 38, with a few sheds and a greenhouse, and a bridge approach where Maple Place crosses the creek at the bottom left. Main Street's cross streets West Cross and West Warren are lettered in the right margin as pointers to sheet 4.
notes: Front Street West is today West Front Street; the modern West Front Street nodes at Main Street and at Broadway lie 8 to 12 m from the drawn junctions and were left out of the fit.
Maple Place carries the older name West Mott in brackets.
The Surf Theatre and the Keyport Weekly printing office stand on Front Street.

The sheet is split into two parts at Luppatatong Creek: the blocks west of the creek fit the modern streets only when placed separately (one part fitted 6.6 m RMSE at 3.73 px/ft against 1.4 m and 4.02 px/ft for this part alone).

100 ft. Front St W., Beers, Kearney, Barnes, Stout, Short, W. Elizabeth, Maple Pl to Main; Broadway area west of Luppatatong Creek. Two parts: 1 (east of the creek, main) and 2 (Broadway, Chingarora and Luppatatong Avs west of the creek), split because the two areas do not fit the modern streets together.

sheet-6-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 6, west of Luppatatong Creek, covers the blocks along Broadway between the creek mouth on Raritan Bay and Chingarora and Luppatatong Avenues, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the grid turned about 20 degrees. Washington runs along the left edge and Broadway diagonally through the middle, crossed by 1st Street at the top and by Front Street, which leaves Broadway and runs down to the bridge over the creek at the right. Below, 1st Street and 2nd Street cross Chingarora Avenue and Luppatatong Avenue in long narrow lots running down towards the creek (blocks 145 and 150). The buildings are frame dwellings of one and a half to two storeys with sheds and auto garages, and a few stores at the corner of Broadway and Front Street. Large blocks 205 and 37 between Broadway and the creek are mostly empty land. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches run along Broadway, Washington and Front Street. Sheet 5 adjoins on the left.
notes: 1st Street west of Broadway is today West 1st Street, and between Chingarora and Luppatatong Avenues Northwest 1st Street; 2nd Street is West 2nd Street.
Placed separately from the rest of the sheet: it does not fit the modern streets together with the blocks east of the creek. Three detected junctions only (an exact fit); low confidence.

100 ft. Front St W., Beers, Kearney, Barnes, Stout, Short, W. Elizabeth, Maple Pl to Main; Broadway area west of Luppatatong Creek. Two parts: 1 (east of the creek, main) and 2 (Broadway, Chingarora and Luppatatong Avs west of the creek), split because the two areas do not fit the modern streets together.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-west corner of Keyport, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page; the borough line runs down the left edge. In the upper part Maple Place, continuing west as Matawan Road, crosses the sheet, with Washington and an unnamed street north of it and the blocks of Chingarora Avenue, Luppatatong Avenue and the unopened 5th Street to the east. Broadway runs diagonally from Maple Place to Clark at the bottom left, with Gaston, Geran, Wooley, Center and a second unnamed street laid out in narrow lots west of it. The built-up part is thin: frame dwellings along Maple Place and Matawan Road, a Catholic church and a plumber's shop west of Broadway, the private garage and offices of the Rollo Trucking Corporation at the corner of Broadway and Maple Place, and scattered houses on Chingarora and Luppatatong Avenues. Most of the lower half is open land: the large blocks 224 and 233 on either side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which crosses the sheet diagonally, and the meanders of Luppatatong Creek. In the lower right corner Monroe, Adams, Madison and Jefferson outline the blocks of the south-east grid, with a single row of six apartments on Monroe. Clark runs along the bottom edge beside the borough line.
notes: Matawan Road is lettered in brackets as the continuation of Maple Place; both are Maple Place today.
5th Street between Chingarora and Luppatatong Avenues is marked not opened.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey line across the sheet is today the Henry Hudson Trail.
Broadway near Maple Place and the Maple Place / Orchard Street junction were rebuilt around the NJ 35 interchange and were left out of the fit; Adams is today NJ 36 in part.

100 ft. South-west: Maple Pl (Matawan Rd), Broadway, Washington, Geran, Wooley, Gaston, Center, Chingarora and Luppatatong Avs, CRR of NJ, Luppatatong Creek, Monroe/Adams/Madison/Jefferson corner; borough line on the left. Area rebuilt around NJ 35; one part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the southern part of central Keyport, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. Maple Place, with the older name West Mott in brackets, runs along the top; Main Street lies along the right edge, where the sheet joins sheet 9, and Monroe Street, lettered Not Opened in its eastern part, runs along the foot. Between them Cass, Perry and Beers Streets run down the sheet, crossed by Walling Terrace, Francis, Washington, Jackson, St. George Place and St. Peters Place, and Kearney Street runs down the right-hand side. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. The principal industries are the Whitall Tatum Company, makers of druggists' sundries and rubber goods, whose brick mill buildings stand beside Francis Street at the left and are described in a long note on watchman, hydrants and fire pails, and, further down at the left edge, the Architectural Tile and Faience Company with its kilns and machine shop. A small light station stands beside the railroad. Most other blocks (numbered 159 to 193) are platted but empty: narrow lots drawn in outline with no buildings, notably the large blocks 181 and 187 between St. George and St. Peters Places, while frame dwellings stand along Perry and Beers Streets near Walling Terrace and Jackson Street, and a range of greenhouses stands near Kearney Street at the right. A creek winds across the upper left corner with a bridge, and a compass rose stands near it. Several streets are lettered Not Opened. Street widths of 40, 50 and 80 feet are lettered. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 5, 6, 7 and 9, and a scale bar stands at the foot.
notes: Maple Place is lettered with the older name West Mott in brackets.
Washington on this sheet is today Pershing Place; Beers, Perry, Cass, Kearney and Monroe are today Beers Street, Perry Street, Cass Street, Kearney Street and Monroe Street.
Maple Place at the top of the sheet was not used as control because the modern line near Beers Street is displaced from the drawn one.
Modern nodes Beers Street / Francis Street (12 m), Kearney Street / Walling Terrace (16 m) and Beers Street / Saint George Place (6 m) disagree with the drawn junctions and were rejected by the fit.
100 ft, one part. Cass, Perry, Beers, Kearney, Walling Terrace, Francis, Washington (now Pershing Place), Jackson, Monroe, St. George and St. Peters Pls, Main; CRR of NJ.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the south-eastern part of central Keyport, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. Maple Place, with the older name West Mott in brackets, runs along the top of the sheet; Main Street forms the left edge, and Broad Street, Division Street, Osborn Street, Atlantic Street, Church Street and Van Dorn Street run down the sheet, crossed by Butler, Hurley, Union, Jackson and Monroe Streets, with Adams at the foot. Atlantic Street and Van Dorn Street run obliquely, and Conover and Florence Avenue are lettered at the lower right, where a creek runs down to the shore of Florence Avenue. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the top left diagonally. Near the top stand the Louis Stultz Jr. flour and coal works and ice plant, the Conover Lumber Company yard with its lumber shed, wood-working shop and a long pipe note on its fire protection, a passenger station and a garage along the railroad, and a Baptist church with a lumber yard at the upper right. Frame dwellings line Broad, Division and Osborn Streets and the upper ends of Church and Van Dorn Streets. Over the lower two thirds of the sheet the blocks, numbered 101 to 138, are platted but largely empty: they are shown in outline with lot lines and a few scattered houses and outbuildings, and the blocks at the foot carry only a handful of buildings. Street widths of 40 and 50 feet are lettered. Dashed lines show water pipes of 4 and 6 inches. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 4, 8, 10 and 13, and a compass rose and the scale bar stand at the right and lower left.
notes: Maple Place is lettered with the older name West Mott in brackets.
Union Street is drawn with its north edge only; the south side is left blank, and Union Street / Osborn Street fits 3 m from the other control.
Main Street changes direction at Monroe Street on the sheet, and the modern Main Street / Monroe Street node is 3.5 m from a fit to the other points.

Main, Broad, Division, Osborn, Atlantic, Church and Van Dorn are today Main Street, Broad Street, Division Street, Osborn Street, Atlantic Street, Church Street and Van Dorn Street; Butler, Hurley, Jackson and Monroe are the same with Street added.
Adams is not in OpenStreetMap under that name; NJ 36 runs on or near its line.
100 ft, one part. Main, Broad, Division, Osborn, Atlantic, Church, Van Dorn, Conover, Butler, Hurley, Union, Jackson, Monroe, Adams (now NJ 36); Louis Stultz Jr. ice plant, Conover Lumber Co.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the eastern part of Keyport from Atlantic Street and the Raritan Bay shore to Fulton Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 21 degrees on the page. At the left a strip of regular blocks lies between Osborn and Atlantic Streets, with Church Street between them, crossed by 3rd Street (Cross) East, East Warren and East Elizabeth Streets and by Maple Place with its old name West Mott in brackets at the foot. The rest of the sheet is a diagonal grid: 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets East run obliquely down the sheet and are crossed by Harrison, Green Grove Avenue, Prospect, Myrtle Avenue, Waverly and Fulton Streets and, further south, by Manchester Avenue and 5th and 7th Streets East. The northern edge is the bay shore, a heavy line with blue tint, with East Front Street, a dock and the Keyport Yacht Club and the Keyport Dry Dock Company, a marine and auto repairing and general machine works with bench and machine shops, standing on it. The central district is built up with frame dwellings, shops and a public school, No. 2, on 2nd Street East. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and a spur cross the lower middle with a mill work and lumber premises and the large Reliance Tire and Rubber Corporation works near Maple Place, with its power and light buildings, and the Canover Lumber Company yard stands near Atlantic Street at the left. Large blocks numbered 4 to 9, 51, 57, 108 to 124 and 201 and 202 divide the sheet, and the eastern edge near Fulton Street and Waverly Street is only partly built. A compass rose stands at the upper left. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 3, 4, 9 and 11, and the scale note is at the top right.
notes: East Front is today East Front Street; 1st, 2nd and 3rd Street East are today 1st Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street.

Harrison is today the north end of Green Grove Avenue (OpenStreetMap has Green Grove Avenue junctions with 1st, 2nd and 3rd Street on its line; the Harrison Avenues in the extract are in Matawan and Union Beach).
East Elizabeth and East Warren are today Elizabeth Street and Warren Street; Maple Place is lettered with the older name West Mott in brackets.

The fit leaves residuals of 2 to 4 m with a systematic pattern along Atlantic Street (north points about 3 m one way, south points about 3 m the other), which suggests the sheet is slightly stretched; a second-order fit cut the leave-one-out error from 2.6 to 2.1 m.
Modern 7th Street / Green Grove Avenue is 11.6 m from the drawn junction and was rejected.

100 ft, one part. Osborn/Church/Atlantic strip and the diagonal grid of 1st-7th Sts E, Harrison (now Green Grove Av north of 3rd), Green Grove, Manchester, Waverly, Prospect, Myrtle, Fulton; residuals of 2 to 4 m with a pattern along Atlantic (sheet slightly stretched; not split).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the far eastern edge of Keyport, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 22 degrees on the page. The Raritan Bay shore crosses the top, and at its left stands the Keyport Water Works, with its filter beds, pumps and a note on its six artesian wells, steam pumps and standpipe. Myrtle Avenue, Cedar Street and Waverly and Fulton Streets run down the left side of the sheet, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey running between Cedar Street and Waverly Street, and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets cross them towards the right. Pine Street, Oak Street and Spring Street lead off diagonally into the middle of the sheet; Walnut Street runs diagonally across the upper right, with Oak Place, Locust Avenue and Howard Street also lettered. The densest building is in the strip along 1st and 2nd Streets and near Fulton Street, with frame dwellings, shops, a fire department and freight house, the Lincoln Hose Company, a lumber company yard and Steiner and Son's coal works beside the railroad. East and north of these streets the lots are platted in long narrow strips with houses scattered along them, and the large blocks numbered 31 to 35, 50, 57, 102, 103, 107, 230 and 231 are mostly blank. The lower half is open ground crossed by a second railroad line and by the winding Chingarora Creek, with only a row of houses along Fulton Street. A compass rose stands at the upper right and a scale note and scale bar are on the sheet. Street widths of 30, 35 and 40 feet are lettered. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 10 and 12.
notes: East Front is today East Front Street; Myrtle Avenue, Cedar, Pine, Oak, Walnut, Waverly, Fulton, Spring Street and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Street are today the same names with Street or Avenue added.
Modern Locust Street / Walnut Street is about 30 m from the drawn Locust Avenue and was not used as control.
The junction of 3rd Street and Waverly Street lies on blank paper at the left edge and was excluded; it is drawn on sheet 10.
Howard and Oak Place are not in the modern street data.
100 ft, one part. Myrtle Av, Cedar, Pine, Oak, Spring, Walnut, Waverly, Fulton, 1st-3rd Sts, Howard, Locust Av; Keyport Water Works; Chingarora Creek.

sheet-12-1.description: The main part of sheet 12, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Walnut Street runs straight down the left edge of the page (north lies about 60 degrees clockwise of the top), shows the works of the Aeromarine Plane and Motor Company on the east side of Keyport, between Walnut Street and the mouth of Chingarora Creek. The plant is a group of large tile-roofed buildings in pink: the final assembly room with stock and drafting rooms, a machine shop with wing varnishing and covering on the second floor, machine shops with auto paint and motor assembling, a bumper department, a dry kiln, a wood mill and pattern department, a foundry and a boiler house, with a separate steel hangar, an experimental department and a long frame boat shop to the east. A note gives the fire protection: watchmen day and night, electric light and power, steam heat, three outside hydrants and a 60 gallon chemical tank mounted on a Ford chassis. A landing field is marked to the north-east beyond Locust. Along Walnut Street and the private lane Oak Place (marked arbitrary, 18 feet wide) are frame dwellings, the plant offices, a gate house, a raw stock shed and a millwright shop. Pine Street and Oak Street are drawn only as short pointers on the far side of Walnut Street, which belongs to sheet 11. Chingarora Creek crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally; a heavy line below it separates this part from the inset of the Broad Street wharves.
notes: Aeromarine Plane and Motor Company works (seaplanes and motors), with a landing field to the north-east.
Oak Place is marked arbitrary (a private name), 18 feet wide; it does not survive as a public street.

Placed from hand-picked points: Pine Street and Oak Street at Walnut Street (drawn only as pointers) and a parcel block corner at Walnut and Locust; the modern Locust Street / Walnut Street node is about 30 m from the drawn junction and was not used.

50 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: 1 Aeromarine Plane and Motor works between Walnut St and Chingarora Creek (turned, north about 60 deg clockwise of up); 2 inset of the Broad Street steamboat wharves on Raritan Bay (north near up).

sheet-12-2.description: The lower right part of sheet 12, separated from the Aeromarine works above by a heavy line, is an inset of the Keyport waterfront at the north end of Broad Street on Raritan Bay, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. Broad Street, 50 feet wide, runs up from 1st Street to the shore, with water pipes along it. On the bay are the wharves of two steamboat lines: the New York and New Jersey Steamboat Company, with freight houses Nos. 1 and 2 on a pier enclosing a slip, and to the east, across a creek inlet, the freight house of the Keansburg Steamboat Company, reached by a 425 foot walk. On the west side of Broad Street stand the Bayside Hotel bar and a few frame buildings and sheds; block numbers 1, 2 and 3 tie the inset to sheet 2, which covers the same blocks to the south. Much of the inset is open water of Raritan Bay and the mouth of the creek. The pier areas are hatched in yellow as frame platforms.
notes: Wharves of the New York and New Jersey Steamboat Company and the Keansburg Steamboat Company.
The shore here has been filled since; American Legion Drive now runs along the waterfront north of 1st Street.
Placed from one detected junction (Broad Street / 1st Street) with the scale of sheet 4 and the rotation of its measured lines: low confidence away from that corner.

50 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line: 1 Aeromarine Plane and Motor works between Walnut St and Chingarora Creek (turned, north about 60 deg clockwise of up); 2 inset of the Broad Street steamboat wharves on Raritan Bay (north near up).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers South Keyport, the edge of town south of Adams Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 20 degrees on the page. Adams runs along the top, with Division Street lettered as a pointer to sheet 9 above. Broad comes down the left side and bends south-east to become Main, which runs diagonally across the sheet to a five-way junction at the bottom where Clark Road, Florence Avenue and a road south along Chingarora Creek meet it. Atlantic and Van Dorn Avenue run down the right half, and Florence Avenue crosses the lower right corner diagonally; Center (Wausau) is a short street west of Main. Much of the sheet is open land: large blocks 46, 45, 193, 232 and 48 are almost empty, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds along Main, Atlantic and Van Dorn Avenue. The buildings of note are the Keyport Laundry Company on Broad near Adams (concrete floor, electric power and lights, steam heat), the Liberty Hose Company fire house on Main, a paint shop and stores along Main, storage buildings beside Chingarora Creek at Florence Avenue, and the private garage, auto repair shop and office of Ackerman Bros. trucking at the bottom by the creek. Chingarora Creek winds across the lower centre and runs up the right side of the sheet beside Florence Avenue. The title South Keyport is lettered near the top right.
notes: Adams is not in OpenStreetMap; NJ 36 runs along its line today.
Center (Wausau) is today Center Street; Clark Road is Clark Street; Van Dorn Avenue is Van Dorn Street.
The road along Chingarora Creek south of the five-way junction is today Holmdel Road.
The area has been rebuilt around the NJ 35 and NJ 36 interchange; the modern junctions fit the sheet only to about 4 m.
50 ft (scale bar). South Keyport: Adams (now NJ 36), Broad, Main, Atlantic, Van Dorn Av, Florence Av, Center (Wausau), Clark Road, Chingarora Creek; one part.
